mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25 percentage points, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the threshold in the expected direction.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 0.5% is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return, reflecting optimism about labor market strength and economic expansion.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite PAYEMS exceeding the threshold (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (industrial production) exceeds the prior quarter's average by at least 2%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, signaling robust production momentum.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days despite the production signal (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of 3% or more over two consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (previous month) and INDPRO < (two months prior)
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or indistinguishable from baseline during the two-month INDPRO decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 6% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be positive, reflecting reduced labor market friction and investor optimism.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 6.0 and UNRATE < previous two months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the three-month UNRATE decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the same month are associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual demand signals.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both proxies meet the trigger (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.4% month-over-month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to inflationary pressure dampening equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during the inflation spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: If INDPRO remains below its 2017 average for four consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is expected to be negative, reflecting persistent supply-side constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (2017 average) for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the four-month INDPRO weakness (p < 0.05).
